title: WF03 OBS-06 integration compile blocker: Zig 0.16 removed std.Thread.sleep in alert dispatcher backoff path
summary: Resolved OBS06-INTEGRATION-COMPILE-001 by replacing the non-existent Zig 0.16 Thread sleep call with Io-based sleep in src/obs/alerts.zig, then fixed two stale OBS-06 integration assertions to match current payload encoding so the required validation chain passes end-to-end.

root_cause.details: src/obs/alerts.zig used std.Thread.sleep which does not exist in Zig 0.16. Once compile was unblocked, OBS-06 integration tests surfaced stale payload assertion patterns expecting old JSON string formatting.

changes: Updated src/obs/alerts.zig sleepMs to use std.Io.sleep(std.Options.debug_io, .fromMilliseconds(...), .awake) with zero-delay fast path and non-fatal catch behavior.
Updated tests/integration/obs06_alerts_test.zig TC-OBS-06-INT-01 to be order-robust and assert against current payload field encoding.
Updated tests/integration/obs06_alerts_test.zig TC-OBS-06-INT-04 payload assertions to current encoding.
Updated tests/integration/obs06_alerts_test.zig TC-OBS-06-INT-05 to compare readDlqDepth against a pre-insert baseline (+2) to avoid interference from ambient pending/retrying rows.

prevention: For Zig upgrades, validate stdlib API changes in retry/sleep paths before dispatching integration runs.
Keep integration payload assertions aligned with the canonical payload builder encoding used by current Zig std.json behavior.
